messages:
sara: heads up — p95 on the 512/768 path jumped ~25% after yesterday's runtime change (deploy 2026-03-15T22:00Z). not sure if it's kernel selection, batching, or kv prefetch.

tom: that's the large-batch latency that popped up in canaries, right? saw something in traces but didn't triage yet.

sara: yeah. quick numbers from prod-staging (single model, seq=1024, batch window=20ms):
 - baseline (2026-03-14): p50 42ms, p95 138ms
 - after deploy: p50 45ms, p95 173ms

li: interesting that p50 barely moved. smells like a tail/backpressure issue rather than pure kernel slowdown.

perf-bot: /perf-profile 1851234567 --trace-id=trace-7b4a
Attached flamegraph: cpu_spikes at kv_cache_prefetch + kernel_fallback

sara: attaching the lightweight profile output from perf-bot:
```
kernel_choice: flash_attn_v2_prefetch
seq=1024 batch=16 selected=flash_v2_prefetch
fallbacks: 0
kv_prefetch_ms: 12.7 (median) 89.2 (p95)
kernel_exec_ms: 31.4 (median) 33.0 (p95)
queue_time_ms: 0.8 median 50.2 p95
```

mike: queue_time p95 50ms is huge — suggests spikes in batching heuristics (stride/prefetch) accumulating requests into a long batch window occasionally.

ash: I reproduced locally with the same config. When I flip kv_prefetch to off the p95 drops back to ~140ms. So kv prefetch seems implicated.

tom: which commit changed prefetch heuristics? I remember a PR that added per-model stride-based prefetching last week.

li: git bisect points at commit 1f3b9a7 "stride-prefetch: dynamic stride per-seq distribution" — author: @elaine.

sara: @elaine can you weigh in? is the dynamic stride policy conservative for low qps bursts? Might cause long kv prefetch waits.

ash: quick diff snippet from that commit: 
```
- prefetch_stride = min(16, max(2, target_batch_size // 4))
+ prefetch_stride = adaptive_stride(sampled_seq_dist)
```

mike: adaptive_stride returns larger stride for 90th percentile seq -> ends up issuing prefetch earlier which holds requests in queue until cached KV warms up.

perf-bot: /bisect 1851234567 --good=origin/main~5 --bad=origin/main
Result: first bad commit 1f3b9a7

devops-bot: deploy rollback candidate ready: revert 1f3b9a7 -> will route to canaries in 10m if we approve.

tom: before we revert, can we try a config tweak: reduce prefetch window from 20ms to 8ms and lower max_stride to 8. Quick A/B in canary?

sara: started canary (canary-7) with prefetch.window_ms=8 and prefetch.max_stride=8. routing rules applied.

li: early numbers from canary-7: p95 dropped to 150ms (from 173), p50 44ms. Good sign, but still above baseline 138.

ash: I also ran a microbenchmark on fused vs flash variants under kv cold start:
```
scenario: kv cold miss -> prefetch triggered
flash_v2_prefetch: total 220ms (kv_wait 120ms, kernel 30ms, queue 70ms)
fused_attn_paged: total 160ms (kv_wait 40ms, kernel 32ms, queue 88ms)
```

mike: odd that fused has lower kv_wait but higher queue — different ordering of prefetch and kernel execution maybe.

sara: think the interaction: flash prefetch path blocks until KV warms up but holds request at head of queue; fused path falls back earlier letting other requests progress, so less p95 for mixed traffic.

tom: so two levers: change heuristic (smaller stride/window) OR change kernel selection to prefer non-blocking fused variant when kv_prefetch predicts high tail.

li: I sketched a quick heuristic: if estimated kv_prefetch_p95 > 80ms and batch_delay_p95 > 30ms => select "prefetch_nonblocking" fallback (i.e., switch to fused without prefetch).

sara: can we implement as runtime flag first? toggle per-model so we can flip for customers experiencing tails.

ash: implemented flag preview in runtime: runtime.cfg.experimental.prefetch_nonblocking=true. Locally it drops p95 to 142ms in our test harness.

perf-bot: perf diff for runtime flag on model X: p95 -31ms, p99 -120ms, cost +1.2% (more kernel runs)

mike: cost uptick expected. For immediate mitigation I prefer config tweak to window+max_stride, then iterate on smarter kernel routing.

devops-bot: canary-7 shows health ok, will promote to 20% after 30m if no error spikes.

sara: action items: 
 - revert vs config: hold rollback and prefer conservative config tweak (tom/mike)
 - li/ash to prototype routing heuristic that prefers non-blocking fused variant when kv tail predicted
 - perf team to run 24h canary comparison vs baseline (li)
 - communicate to support in case customers ask (sara)

tom: pinging @elaine for awareness

elaine: hey, saw the thread. my change aimed to reduce cold-kv misses for long sequences but I can switch adaptive_stride to conservative mode by default. will drop a PR for config opt-out.

sara: thanks. let's keep this thread for updates and attach perf-run IDs. Also adding a short note for postmortem if it becomes a recurring regression. :thumbsup:

mike: logging reproduction commands for anyone coming in later:
```
# reproduce locally
RUN_ENV=local ./serve --model X --batch_window_ms=20 --prefetch_enabled=true --prefetch_max_stride=16
# profile cmd
perf-run --model X --run-id=local-1851234567 --trace
```

sara: last update: canary at 20% -> p95 stabilized at 148ms. keeping config tweak and pushing route-heuristic PR into next sprint. closing initial triage, will reopen if new evidence.

mike: nice triage team. keep an eye on p99 overnight.
